cases.sentence: – Тут у вас болотце есть, возле ___.
cases.explain: «осиновой рощи» — after the preposition «возле», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "To a marsh beside an aspen coppice. By the way, Arkady, I flushed five head of woodcock. Perhaps you would like to go and shoot them?"

cases.explain: «естественными науками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "Yes, I prefer physics—in fact, the natural sciences in general—to anything else."

cases.sentence: – Вы столь ___ о немцах? – проговорил с изысканною учтивостью Павел Петрович.
cases.explain: «высокого мнения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "You think highly of the Germans?" Paul Petrovitch's tone was now studiously polite, for he was beginning to feel irritated with the man—his aristocratic nature could not altogether stomach Bazarov's absolute lack of ceremony, the fact that this doctor's son not only knew no diffidence, but actually returned snappish and reluctant answers, and infused a brusquerie akin to rudeness into his tone. "At least the savants of that part of the world have some energy in them," retorted Bazarov.

cases.explain: «дельный народ» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: "Quite so. And your opinion of our Russian savants is—well, perhaps less flattering?"

cases.sentence: – Не все, – ответил с ___ Базаров, которому явно не хотелось продолжать словопрение.
cases.explain: «коротким зевком» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "No, not all Germans," replied Bazarov with a passing yawn. Clearly he had no mind to continue the controversy. Meanwhile Paul Petrovitch glanced at Arkady as much as to say: "Admit that your friend has beautiful manners!"

cases.sentence: О ___ я уже не упоминаю: известно, что это за птицы.
cases.explain: «русских немцах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: "For my own part," he continued, ostentatiously, and with an effort, "I, a fallible mortal, do not favour the Germans. Of course, I am not including in that category the Russo-Germans, who, as we know, are birds of passage. Rather, it is the Germans of Germany proper whom I cannot abide. Once upon a time they used to produce men like Schiller and like—what's his name?—Goethe: for both of which authors my brother has a marked predilection. But now the German nation has become a nation solely of chemists and materialists."

cases.sentence: Но и ___ мне не по нутру.
cases.explain: «немецкие немцы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "For my own part," he continued, ostentatiously, and with an effort, "I, a fallible mortal, do not favour the Germans. Of course, I am not including in that category the Russo-Germans, who, as we know, are birds of passage. Rather, it is the Germans of Germany proper whom I cannot abide. Once upon a time they used to produce men like Schiller and like—what's his name?—Goethe: for both of which authors my brother has a marked predilection. But now the German nation has become a nation solely of chemists and materialists."

cases.sentence: – ___ в двадцать раз полезнее всякого поэта, – перебил Базаров.
cases.explain: «Порядочный химик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "A good chemist is worth a score of your poets," remarked Bazarov.

cases.sentence: Ну, а насчет других, в людском быту принятых, постановлений вы придерживаетесь такого же ___?
cases.explain: «отрицательного направления» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "Very good. And, with regard to such other postulates as usually are granted in human affairs, the attitude which you adopt is negative in the same degree?"

cases.sentence: С своей стороны, я очень рад, что вы занимаетесь ___.
cases.explain: «естественными науками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "Nay, we will debate the subject later," he said. "And then, while recognising your views, good Evgenii Vasilitch, we will state our own. Individually speaking, I am delighted that you should be interested in the natural sciences. For instance, I am told that recently Liebig[1] has made some surprising discoveries in the matter of the improvement of soils. Consequently you might be able to help me in my agricultural labours, and to give me much useful advice."

cases.sentence: Я слышал, что Либих[26] сделал ___ насчет удобрений полей.
cases.explain: «удивительные открытия» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: – Да, – проговорил он, ни на кого не глядя, – беда пожить этак годков пять в деревне, в отдалении от ___!
cases.explain: «великих умов» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "Yes," he said, without looking at any one in particular, "it is indeed a terrible thing to have lived five years in the country, and to have stood remote from superior intellects! If one is ab origine a fool, one becomes so more than ever, seeing that, however much one may try not to forget what one has learnt, there will dawn upon one, sooner or later, the revelation that one's knowledge is all rubbish, that sensible men have ceased to engage in such futilities, and that one has lagged far behind the times. But, in such a case, what is one to do? Evidently the younger generation know more than we do."

cases.sentence: Ты стараешься не забыть того, чему тебя учили, а там – хвать! – оказывается, что все это вздор, и тебе говорят, что ___ этакими пустяками больше не занимаются и что ты, мол, отсталый колпак.[28] Что делать!
cases.explain: «путные люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

But, in such a case, what is one to do? Evidently the younger generation know more than we do."

cases.sentence: Я нашел довольно ___ водяного жука, Dytiscus marginatus, знаешь?
cases.explain: «редкий экземпляр» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: "What? Am I to fawn upon these rustic aristocrats, even though their attitude is one purely of conceit and subservience to custom? If such be Paul Petrovitch's bent, he had better have continued his career in St. Petersburg. Never mind him, however. Do you know, I have found a splendid specimen of the water beetle dytiscus marginatus. Are you acquainted with it? I will show it you."
